_comment: FDA copy perimeter. Do not loosen without product and legal sign-off. lint.py fails on any user_facing_prohibited pattern in a user-facing string under scan_paths (the app and Watch sources and both string catalogues); coach_response_prohibited applies to Flo's replies. See docs/VOICE_AND_TOOL_USE.md.

Diagnosis is a regulated medical-device function. Use 'observation' or 'pattern'. Methodology page and HealthDisclaimerView may use 'does not diagnose' (allowlisted). 'arrhythmia' implies a cardiac diagnosis. Describe the signal ('irregular beats') without naming the condition. The phrase 'respiratory sinus arrhythmia' is a physiology term and is exempted via the lookbehind.
Diagnostic term. Describe the observation and its range, not a pathology.
clinical-sounding diagnostic label. Describe as 'reduced beat-to-beat variability' or similar.
clinical diagnostic label. Describe as 'elevated respiration' or 'reduced breath quality' instead.
clinical-physiology label that reads as a diagnosis to lay users; describe behaviour instead.
AFib is a regulated cardiac diagnosis. Refer questions to the Apple Watch ECG app via the standard refusal.
Naming a cardiac condition is a regulated diagnosis. Describe the signal, not the condition.
Naming a cardiac condition is a regulated diagnosis.
Naming a cardiac condition is a regulated diagnosis. 'Low overnight heart rate' is the observation.
Naming a cardiac condition is a regulated diagnosis. 'Elevated heart rate' is the observation.

Clinical diagnosis.
Blood-pressure diagnosis; the app does not measure blood pressure.
Categorical autonomic-state claim. HRV is consistent with a state; it does not establish one.
Asserts the metric reveals a true internal state. Say what the value is consistent with.
Emphatic identity claim about physiology. Describe the association, not an identity.
Implies a finding the app cannot establish. Point at what to check instead.
Categorical recovery verdict. Report the range the value sits in.
Certainty language about the user's physiological state.
asserts a reading can carry training load. The DFA band it described is a product convention, not a validated readiness scale. Describe the range.
promotes a wellness threshold to a clinical one. Apple states Apple Watch blood-oxygen readings are not intended for medical use; call a conservative product rule what it is.
told the reader their own metric was fake on the strength of an unvalidated band. Report the range, not a ranking of which reading is real.
ranks one reading as more real than another. 'Organized Recovery' alone is the window-classification LABEL and is deliberately still allowed.
claims illness detection. Deviations from baseline are context, not a warning system.
prediction claim. The resp-rate + temperature rule has not been prospectively validated.

slow or paced breathing does NOT raise HF under the app's fixed bands. 5.5 breaths/min is 0.09 Hz; HF is 0.15-0.40 Hz (9-24 breaths/min). The enlarged oscillation moves INTO LF and HF falls. Literal alternatives rather than \w+ so check_perimeter_sync can synthesise a probe. This claim appeared three times across two articles and survived one round of correction, which is why it is a pattern and not an edit.

evasion of the banned prediction vocabulary rather than a change of claim. The perimeter forbade 'strong predictor' and cause detection shipped 'strongly suggests' and 'strong indicator' of immune activation. Assert the observation, not its strength.
a likelihood claim about infection. Prospective wearable illness alerts have a positive predictive value of roughly 4-10% — most are not infections. Name the pattern, not the diagnosis.
implies a base rate the evidence does not support. Most instances of these patterns are not followed by illness.
categorical autonomic claim that slipped past the 'clear X dominance' rule by reordering the words. Same claim, same problem.
a composite score that is calibrated rather than outcome-validated cannot certify full recovery. Describe the position against the user's own range.

App Store 1.4.1 illness framing: no rule in this app has been evaluated against illness outcomes, and the Help Center's own citation puts the positive predictive value of far better wearable alerts at 4-9%. Do not assert that illness is likely; list common causes, illness last.

A cause titled 'Possible Illness' or 'Possible Immune Response' is a diagnosis in a headline. Title the physiology ('Sharp HRV Drop').

App Store 1.4.1 illness framing: no rule in this app has been evaluated against illness outcomes, and the Help Center's own citation puts the positive predictive value of far better wearable alerts at 4-9%. 'Monitor for symptoms' is a clinical directive that presumes an illness. At most: 'if you feel unwell, rest, and talk to a clinician about symptoms that concern you'.

App Store 1.4.1 illness framing: no rule in this app has been evaluated against illness outcomes, and the Help Center's own citation puts the positive predictive value of far better wearable alerts at 4-9%. Claims that a pattern appears before cold/flu symptoms, or before people feel, report or notice being unwell or get sick, are illness prediction: a lead time this app has never measured (VitalsScoring.calculateVitalsScore forbids stating one). The second half was added after Help shipped 'often appears a day or two before people report feeling unwell', which the cold/flu-only pattern let through.

App Store 1.4.1: blood glucose is one of the measurements the guideline names, and nothing this app reads (heart rate, HRV, sleep, Apple Health vitals) supports inferring it. Cause copy said low HRV 'can indicate dehydration or low blood sugar'. Describe what was measured and common everyday causes ('a long gap since eating') instead.

_allowlist_strings_note: Exact user-facing strings, and string-catalog keys with all their translations, exempt from every pattern: approved disclaimers whose negated form has to name a prohibited term (for example 'not ... diagnosis'), and the software sense of a word whose translation the multilingual patterns cannot tell from the medical one (Italian 'Diagnostica avanzata', Arabic 'سجل تشخيص' for a diagnostic log).
allowlist_strings: The developer receives only what you choose to email: a support request, an AI reply you report, or a diagnostic log you share.
Before each sentence of a reply is shown or spoken, the app removes sentences that make diagnostic claims or contain offensive English words
For wellness and fitness use only. Not a medical device; not medical advice, diagnosis, or treatment.
AI responses are informational coaching from the data this app collected. They are not medical diagnosis or treatment. For health decisions, talk to a qualified clinician.
Active. Refuses AFib / arrhythmia / symptom queries before any provider call.
Emuqu is not a medical device. It is not FDA-approved, FDA-cleared, or certified by any regulatory body.

This app does not provide medical advice, diagnosis, or treatment. Nothing in this app should be interpreted as a recommendation to begin, modify, or discontinue any exercise program, medical treatment, or health-related activity.

Emuqu doesn't detect AFib or arrhythmia — it isn't a medical device. If you're worried about your heart rhythm, talk to your doctor. Apple Watch has a clinically validated ECG feature that's designed for that specific purpose.

Talk to your doctor about that. I can't assess your health — Emuqu is a fitness coaching app, not a medical device. If you're feeling unwell, please contact a clinician (or your local emergency number for severe symptoms).
Emuqu does not predict injury, diagnose any condition, or replace clinical judgment.
Emuqu voorspelt geen blessures, stelt geen diagnoses en vervangt geen klinisch oordeel.
_allowlist_paths_note: Files whose text is machine-facing: regex guard patterns, intent-routing keyword lists and model-facing safety rules that quote a banned term in order to forbid it. The lexicon entry is a family prefix, so a file split stays covered.
_negation_guards_note: A prohibited phrase quoted inside a prohibition ('Never tell the user that a number "predicts injury"') is allowed. The guards key on the surrounding sentence, so they survive renames and file splits. Swift source only.
